Ratne Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volynska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This, the older of Ratne's two Jewish cemeteries, was established in the early 18th century; per the 1938-published memoirs of Fishel Heler of Ratno, an old cemetery was founded during the community's reconstruction after the Great Northern War of 1706–07, and held a mass grave of war victims from that conflict. According to local tradition, one of the first Hasidim, Tzvi ben Dov of Mihnovka, known as the Maggid of Ratne, lived in the town, and the Hasidic mystic Leib ben Sarah taught in the local beit-midrash. By 1897, the Jewish population reached 2,219 (71.8 percent); Neskhizh Hasids were also present. During the 1942 ghetto's liquidation, around 2,000 Jews were executed, following the murder of 120 more in retaliation for partisan attacks. This cemetery was demolished by Soviet authorities after WWII and later overbuilt with residences and a pharmacy.
